title: Washington: termination and nonrenewal do not use the same exit rule
description: Build separate cause, cure, compensation and territory records before changing a covered franchise relationship.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the actual statutory relationship
paragraphs: RCW 19.100.010 includes oral or written, express or implied arrangements involving a substantially prescribed or suggested marketing plan, brand association and a franchise fee. Required purchases and training can matter; the fee definition contains specific wholesale, property and other exceptions. Insurance and specified motor-vehicle relationships are treated separately. The federal definition and the word licence do not decide this state test.

sections.heading: An exclusive territory needs an actual boundary
paragraphs: Section 180(2)(f) addresses franchisor competition and competitive grants where the agreement provides an exclusive territory, which must be specified in the agreement. Draw the area, national-account carve-outs, online leads and service obligations before promising exclusivity. The provision does not create an exclusive territory for every franchise. Approved-source purchasing and conduct standards have their own reasonableness/business-ground tests.

sections.heading: A termination has a cause and cure analysis
paragraphs: Section 180(2)(j) restricts termination before expiry to good cause. Its ordinary default branch uses written notice and a reasonable cure opportunity that need not be more than 30 days. Where a default cannot reasonably be cured within 30 days, the text separately addresses substantial and continuing cure action initiated within that time. Do not write an unconditional 30-day minimum or an automatic right to terminate on day 31.

The repeated-breach branch requires three willful and material breaches of the same term within 12 months, with the specified prior notices/opportunities, before the subsequent same-term breach exception. Adjudicated bankruptcy/insolvency, assignment for creditors, voluntary abandonment and the specified business-related criminal outcome have separate immediate-action conditions. Alleging a default does not establish one.

sections.heading: Nonrenewal compensation is a different ledger
paragraphs: Section 180(2)(i) addresses fair compensation at expiration for listed assets bought from the franchisor and goodwill, with stated exclusions and offsets. The goodwill exception requires both one year’s notice of nonrenewal and written agreement not to enforce a covenant restraining competition. It does not erase every listed asset obligation. Termination for good cause has its own narrower inventory/supplies purchase rule, including a premises-retention qualification.

sections.heading: Fictional decision: a service territory and a missed standard
paragraphs: Fictional example: a Dutch facilities brand plans to replace a Washington operator after missed response targets while retaining a national customer inside the promised territory. The COO prepares a standards/cause/cure record, a contract territory map and two separate asset ledgers for termination versus expiry. Management cannot select the cheaper ledger merely by relabelling the action.

sections.heading: Keep a decision file
bullets: Confirm this Act’s definitions and relevant Washington connections.
Describe termination, expiry/nonrenewal, competitive entry or another actual action.
Preserve cause, comparators, repeated-breach history and notice/cure evidence.
Separate goodwill from asset-source, condition and offset questions.
Retain settlement/release and other-law questions for their own review.

practicalOutput: A relationship-change matrix with separate territory, cause/cure and termination/nonrenewal compensation records.
limitations: No full damages, limitations-period, federal insolvency or litigation analysis. Section 190 remedies are not a forecast of an award.
No actual agreement, remedy, exemption or planned sale is approved. Federal, sector, employment, tax and local duties remain independent.

title: Wisconsin: a registered franchise still needs a Fair Dealership Law review
description: The dealership definition, exclusions, good cause and separate notice/cure periods answer an operating question.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The operating definition is independent
paragraphs: Chapter 135 defines a dealer as the grantee of a dealership situated in Wisconsin. Its dealership test can involve an express or implied, oral or written agreement granting sale/distribution rights or use of a commercial symbol, with a community of interest. The statutory financial-interest concept needs actual relationship facts. A federal franchise fee analysis or Wisconsin registration receipt does not establish this separate result.

sections.heading: Keep the exclusions visible
paragraphs: Section 135.07 excludes a dealership involving the specified motor-vehicle dealer/distributor/wholesaler acting in that capacity, the insurance business, and door-to-door marketing of goods or services. Liquor has its own provisions. A maintenance brand should record how it actually sells and operates before treating this chapter as a protection or an exemption.

sections.heading: Cause, advance notice and cure are separate
paragraphs: Section 135.03 prohibits covered termination, cancellation, nonrenewal and substantial competitive changes without good cause and puts the cause burden on the grantor. Section 135.04 ordinarily requires 90 days’ prior written notice, all reasons and 60 days to rectify a claimed deficiency; timely rectification voids the notice. Insolvency, assignment for creditors and bankruptcy have stated notice exceptions.

For nonpayment, the statute supplies written default notice and 10 days to remedy from delivery or posting. The official civil jury instruction’s comment expressly preserves 90 days’ advance notice for that branch while shortening cure to 10 days. A 10-day demand should not be entered as an automatic day-11 termination date.

sections.heading: Inventory and remedies require their own evidence
paragraphs: Under 135.045, grantor-initiated termination can trigger, at the dealer’s option, repurchase at fair wholesale market value of qualifying inventories sold by the grantor for resale. The section is confined to merchandise bearing an identifying grantor mark; it is not reimbursement for every computer or operating asset. Section 135.06 provides a conditional damages/costs/fees and injunction route. An injury or award is not presumed from this checklist.

sections.heading: Fictional decision: missed payment and a new competitor
paragraphs: Fictional example: a British grounds-care supplier plans to end a Wisconsin dealer after unpaid invoices and appoint another nearby seller. Its manager first tests dealership/community-of-interest and exclusions, then records cause, default delivery, the separate notice/cure clocks and any substantial competitive change. Finance identifies marked resale stock separately from service tools.

practicalOutput: A dealership-scope and action file with separate 90-day notice, ordinary/nonpayment cure and marked-inventory evidence.
limitations: No independent full appellate opinion was reviewed. The old jury instruction is used for its specific notice explanation alongside the current certified statute.
Arbitration/federal preemption, liquor rules and complete community-of-interest case law remain outside this guide.
No actual agreement, remedy, exemption or planned sale is approved. Federal, sector, employment, tax and local duties remain independent.

title: Virginia: update governing law and post-term competition language for 2026
description: Current law and SCC instructions require a contract/FDD review separate from registration exemptions.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Use the enacted text and its actual scope
paragraphs: The current Retail Franchising Act and SCC’s April 14, 2026 notice confirm that chapters 553 and 554 took effect July 1, 2026. Section 13.1-559 requires a written retail marketing-plan/brand arrangement with a direct or indirect franchise fee of $500 or more, subject to its fee exclusions. The Act applies only where performance contemplates or requires the franchisee to establish or maintain a Virginia place of business. The statute defines that term and contains incidental/ancillary and department exceptions.

sections.heading: The governing-law and competition clauses changed
paragraphs: Section 13.1-559(D) requires Virginia law for franchise contracts offered or entered into pursuant to the Act. Section 13.1-563(A)(4) makes it unlawful to offer or enter a franchise agreement restricting the franchisee’s retail offering, selling or distribution of goods/services after termination or expiration. The text addresses the stated activity and trigger; this guide does not adjudicate confidentiality, intellectual-property or other distinct obligations.

sections.heading: A negotiated franchise sale has a specific exception
paragraphs: Section 563(B) allows the stated restriction where the franchisee sells the franchise at a mutually agreed price to a third party or back to the franchisor, for no more than two years after sale. Preserve the real sale, price, parties and period. Ordinary expiry, a termination label or paying an unrelated invoice does not establish that exception.

sections.heading: A current registration is not the amendment task
paragraphs: The SCC notice calls for the new language in the FDD and agreement, using relevant Item 17 disclosures or a Virginia addendum. For offerings registered before July 1 with later expiry, the agency distinguishes no expected Virginia sale before expiry from a possible or actual sale on/after July 1: the latter requires an amendment application first. Reuse the actual selling entity and approved disclosure version in the sales calendar.

Section 13.1-564 independently restricts cancellation without reasonable cause and undue influence to surrender franchise rights. The 2026 clause changes do not resolve an actual cause dispute. Statutory civil remedies and anti-waiver provisions also require their own trigger and evidence.

sections.heading: Fictional decision: an old template and a November offer
paragraphs: Fictional example: a French services group plans a November 2026 Virginia offer under a registration that began before July. Its template still selects another state’s law and a three-year post-expiry retail restriction. The company secretary maps the Act’s scope, corrects the contract/FDD task and confirms the required amendment before continuing the covered sale process. No conclusion about enforcing an old signed agreement is supplied.

practicalOutput: A Virginia contract/FDD change log with Act scope, sale dates, governing-law language, competition clause and amendment evidence.
limitations: No retroactivity or enforceability conclusion for agreements already signed before July 1, 2026.
Registration exemption, disclosure timing, employee noncompetes, litigation remedies and sector laws remain separate.
No actual agreement, remedy, exemption or planned sale is approved. Federal, sector, employment, tax and local duties remain independent.

title: Connecticut: a franchise exit can also terminate the premises lease
description: The relationship statute has its own definition, cause, notice, premises-service and compensation branches.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The relationship definition does not copy the federal fee test
paragraphs: Section 42-133e describes oral or written marketing-plan/brand arrangements and specific distribution relationships. Its definition does not state a franchise-fee element. The grantor-premises merchandising concession qualification and 42-133h’s agreement-date and Connecticut place-of-business conditions still matter. An answer about the business-opportunity trademark exclusion does not answer this relationship-law question.

sections.heading: Select the notice branch from the facts
paragraphs: Section 42-133f generally requires good cause for termination, cancellation or nonrenewal, including substantial failure/refusal to comply with a material and reasonable obligation. The ordinary written notice states cause and gives at least 60 days. The subsection (e) leased-real-property nonrenewal circumstances instead require six months’ notice; voluntary abandonment has a 30-day branch. The specified serious conviction directly related to the franchise business has an effective-on-delivery-and-written-receipt branch.

These are advance-notice rules with exact conditions. The text reviewed does not supply a universal 60-day cure entitlement or permit a brand to treat an unsupported default allegation as established cause.

sections.heading: The lease can change the service and court file
paragraphs: Where the franchisor leases the premises to the franchisee under a lease ending with the franchise and seeks to terminate that lease, 42-133f(b) requires service by a state marshal or indifferent person and specific lease/right language with the two sections reproduced and attached. Section 42-133g separately addresses continued occupancy, temporary injunctions and the franchisor’s court filings to obtain possession. Sending an ordinary business email is not shown to complete that statutory premises process.

sections.heading: Do not lose the term and inventory questions
paragraphs: Section 42-133f also addresses minimum three-year initial/successive terms for the stated agreements, termination compensation for qualifying inventory/supplies/equipment/furnishings from the franchisor or approved sources, and void waivers, each with conditions. Personalized items without value to the franchisor are excluded from that compensation. Record these issues separately; the notice period does not value the assets or grant a damages award.

sections.heading: Fictional decision: the brand is also the landlord
paragraphs: Fictional example: an overseas technical-services brand leases a Connecticut workshop to its operator and proposes not to renew while changing the site’s use. The COO records the relationship definition and current contract, tests the specific real-property branch, identifies the six-month and service requirements where applicable, and asks finance for eligible asset records. The example does not establish an actual exception or right to possession.

practicalOutput: A Connecticut exit file with separate relationship scope, cause/notice branch, premises-service packet and compensation evidence.
limitations: Source is the official current public mirror of the base code, identical to the 2025 edition; section histories and the available 2026 supplement index were inspected. Later session laws and special-sector overlays are not certified as exhausted.
Petroleum, motor-vehicle and business-opportunity statutes have separate definitions and are not resolved by this page.
No actual agreement, remedy, exemption or planned sale is approved. Federal, sector, employment, tax and local duties remain independent.

title: Florida: the franchise exemption notice does not clear the sales claims
description: Section 817.416 separately addresses intentional misrepresentations about investment, success and market capacity.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: A different section has a different definition
paragraphs: The 2026 text of 817.416 covers a specified commercial franchise/distributorship relationship, express or implied and oral or written. Its four-part definition includes an independent business in a distribution system and substantial reliance on the franchisor for basic goods supply. “Goods” can include articles consumed in an approved service. A pure advisory business is not shown to qualify merely because it uses a brand; a service network supplied with essential consumables requires a more careful factsheet.

sections.heading: Keep three claim files
paragraphs: For a covered sale or establishment, 817.416(2)(a) addresses intentional misrepresentation of prospects/chances of success, known required total investment, and efforts to establish more franchises/distributorships than the market can reasonably sustain. Investment omissions and overexpansion facts therefore deserve their own review, rather than being reduced to whether a document was filed. Preserve the actual audience, statement, omission, knowledge and timing.

sections.heading: The remedy is conditional on a statutory showing
paragraphs: Section 817.416(3) says a person showing a violation in civil court may receive judgment for all money invested; it separately says the court may award reasonable attorney fees and shall award reasonable costs on that showing. This is a conditional statutory route, not a promise of full recovery, an automatic fee award or a general right to cancel every franchise.

sections.heading: Fictional decision: approved consumables and overlapping sales territories
paragraphs: Fictional example: an overseas industrial-cleaning network supplies its operators’ core chemicals and equipment and markets two proposed Florida areas as highly profitable. The expansion team tests the actual four definition elements, records total launch and recurring investment, and prepares demand/capacity evidence for both areas before using the claims. A separate 559.802 notice filing remains a separate task.

sections.heading: Create a representation register
bullets: Map entities, goods and services, supply dependence and distribution rights.
Record success statements and their factual basis, including omissions.
Reconcile the known required total investment with actual sales material.
Compare the proposed outlet count with the defined market-area evidence.
Keep notices, FTC disclosure, consumer protection and sector relationship laws separate.

practicalOutput: A Florida model-and-representation register linking supply reliance, investment, success and market-area statements to actual evidence.
limitations: No universal franchise definition, financial-performance permission, complete consumer-law analysis or state termination protection conclusion.
No actual agreement, remedy, exemption or planned sale is approved. Federal, sector, employment, tax and local duties remain independent.

title: Oregon: an existing franchisee does not make disclosure automatic or unnecessary
description: Renewal, added-unit and resale branches need different change and document evidence.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Begin with the actual state definitions
paragraphs: ORS 650.005 uses a marketing-plan, brand and valuable-consideration franchise test, permits oral or written arrangements, and defines a franchisor as including a subfranchisor selling for $100 or more. The statute’s sale definition separately excludes the stated unchanged uninterrupted renewal/extension. Those details are not a finding that any particular low-fee or amended arrangement is exempt; federal rules and other state branches still need their own tests.

sections.heading: A renewal exception requires three conditions
paragraphs: OAR 441-325-0030(2) covers a renewal, extension, amendment or modification only where there is no interruption in the relationship’s operation, no material change adverse to the franchisee in the relationship, and no material change adverse to the franchisee in previously supplied disclosure information. A familiar operator or an unchanged cover page does not prove all three. Record the actual agreement and disclosure changes.

sections.heading: An additional franchise uses a different test
paragraphs: The additional-unit branch in 0030(3) requires prior disclosure in connection with the earlier sale and no material adverse change in the disclosure information supplied. Do not copy the renewal conditions into an additional-unit checklist or assume the old receipt alone proves current information. When no exception is established, 0020 requires the disclosure and all proposed agreements at least 14 calendar days before the earlier covered agreement or consideration event, including refundable deposits.

sections.heading: Keep resale provisions separate
paragraphs: The franchisee-own-account route in 0030(4) has no-franchisor-involvement, isolated-sale and specified 14-day full-record-access conditions. Rule 0040 separately describes a chapter exemption for the stated own-account/entire-area resale without franchisor participation or aid. Approval rights alone are addressed, but active marketing or assistance can change the facts. This guide does not reconcile every possible overlap or approve a transfer.

sections.heading: Fictional decision: a second service territory and a revised fee
paragraphs: Fictional example: an Irish IT-services brand offers an existing Oregon operator a second territory while changing support charges and financial disclosures. The sales manager compares the prior disclosure with the actual changes and tests the additional-unit branch, rather than marking “renewal — no FDD” because the operator is already known. The resulting record either establishes each selected condition or leaves the ordinary delivery task open.

practicalOutput: A transaction-type and disclosure-change log identifying the exact Oregon renewal, additional-unit or resale branch and missing evidence.
limitations: This is a disclosure/definition decision. Motor-vehicle, fuel, recreational-vehicle and other ongoing-relationship regimes remain outside the guide.
The 2025 official statute and actual current administrative division were read; no current federal monetary exemption threshold is supplied.
No actual agreement, remedy, exemption or planned sale is approved. Federal, sector, employment, tax and local duties remain independent.

title: Washington: review offers, advertising and the operating relationship
description: Washington franchise registration, disclosure, advertising and relationship duties answer different questions.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Begin before a covered offer
paragraphs: RCW 19.100.020 addresses offering as well as selling. A registration or exemption review therefore belongs before a relevant offer, not merely before collecting the initial fee. Washington DFI gives the same starting instruction. The location of a future unit alone does not complete the jurisdiction analysis.

sections.heading: Keep three clocks
paragraphs: The statute contains distinct initial-disclosure, revised-agreement and advertising provisions. Record each event separately rather than putting one “legal paperwork done” date in the launch schedule.

rows: Version delivered, recipient and delivery date
7 calendar days; prospect-initiated negotiations treated separately
File true copy at least 7 days before publication unless shorter period allowed

sections.heading: The agreement needs an operating review
paragraphs: RCW 19.100.180 addresses good faith, purchasing restrictions, exclusive territory, termination and renewal. A national-account carve-out or mandatory supplier is an operating decision to review under those provisions, not just wording to copy from a home-market agreement.

sections.heading: Fictional example: industrial maintenance
paragraphs: A Dutch brand promises an exclusive Washington territory while retaining national accounts. Its COO should define customer allocation, service responsibility, lead routing and revenue entitlement before final drafting. The exercise reveals what requires legal review; it does not decide whether any proposed term is enforceable.

sections.heading: Classify the state arrangement independently
paragraphs: RCW 19.100.010 includes oral/written and implied arrangements, a marketing plan prescribed or suggested in substantial part, substantial brand association and the defined franchise fee. Mandatory goods/services and training charges can matter, while bona fide wholesale, property and other specified payments have exclusions. The state definition has independent insurance and motor-vehicle exclusions; federal classification and the licence label are not substitutes. Separate business-opportunity law is not exhausted here.

sections.heading: Renewal is not the material-change deadline
paragraphs: Under 19.100.070, the ordinary registration and identified exemption-claim period is one year from effectiveness/filing unless the director sets another period. A registration renewal application is due no later than 20 calendar days before expiry. A material adverse condition change or material disclosure change must be amended as soon as reasonably possible and before another franchise sale. Keep the event date, amendment, delivery version and next sale together.

sections.heading: An exit needs a more precise branch
paragraphs: The separate Washington relationship-change guide applies the actual termination, nonrenewal, goodwill/asset, cure and exclusive-territory provisions. Its cause and compensation distinctions should remain separate from this pre-offer calendar.

practicalOutput: A Washington offer and advertising calendar, with a separate contract-operations review.

title: Oregon: no franchise filing approval does not remove disclosure
description: Oregon DFR expressly distinguishes its disclosure and recordkeeping rules from states that approve franchise filings before a sale.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: A narrow answer to a common question
paragraphs: Oregon DFR says it does not require franchisors to file franchise documents and obtain approval before a franchise sale. The same official page says disclosure must be provided at least 14 days before signing a contract or paying money. The absence of this filing process does not mean the offering is outside state law.

sections.heading: Build the evidence trail
paragraphs: DFR also identifies complete books, records and franchise-sale details, including distribution of proceeds. A sales manager should retain which disclosure and agreements were sent, to whom, when, and what money was received. Finance should be able to reconcile proceeds to the transaction.

sections.heading: Fictional example: an Irish IT services business
paragraphs: The team selects Oregon for customer interviews and later considers a branded operator. Its launch worksheet originally contains “registration: none” and no other sales-law tasks. The corrected worksheet records the narrow filing answer and adds the disclosure delivery, document-version and sale-record tasks. Customer procurement, tax nexus and employment remain separate questions.

sections.heading: What this source does and does not establish
paragraphs: The page identifies ORS Chapter 650 and OAR Chapter 441 Division 325, complaint handling and a private civil remedy. It does not establish that every distribution, licensing, professional-services or business-opportunity model has the same outcome. State applicability still depends on the actual facts.
bullets: Record the model and relevant Oregon connections.
Keep the 14-day disclosure clock separate from operational opening milestones.
Assign retention and proceeds-reconciliation responsibility.
Leave unresearched local and sector duties marked unknown.

sections.heading: Use the actual definition and state connections
paragraphs: The 2025 official text of 650.005 describes a marketing-plan, brand and valuable-consideration franchise test and defines franchisor to include a subfranchisor selling for $100 or more. Section 650.015 separately examines offer origin/direction, acceptance and the stated domicile/operation facts. This is an actual state scope screen, not an assumption that only the outlet address matters. Other model and sector regimes remain open.

sections.heading: The current rule includes refundable deposits and all proposed agreements

title: Wisconsin: registration on receipt is not approval of the business
description: Wisconsin describes a same-day, non-merit registration process and a distinct 14-calendar-day disclosure duty.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Two independent prerequisites
paragraphs: Wisconsin DFI says a franchise must be registered no later than its first Wisconsin franchise sale. It describes registration as effective on receipt and expressly says Wisconsin is not a franchise merit-review state. A buyer should not read the registration receipt as validation of the model, projections or management team.

sections.heading: Give disclosure time to run
paragraphs: The agency separately states that an FDD must be supplied 14 calendar days before the earlier of signing a binding franchise or other agreement or payment. Filing on receipt does not start or replace that delivery clock.

sections.heading: Annual filing and material changes
paragraphs: DFI lists a $400 registration fee and one-year effectiveness. It says each franchise system needs a separate filing. Material-event amendments are due within 30 days, with a listed $200 fee, and do not restart the registration year. These amounts were checked against the agency FAQ on the review date and should be rechecked before payment.

sections.heading: Fictional example: facilities and pest-control brands
paragraphs: A group sells two different franchise systems. Its company secretary should establish the separate filing scope, delivery versions and annual dates. A later corporate reorganization is evaluated as a possible material event rather than waiting automatically until next year.

sections.heading: Separate the contract review
paragraphs: The FAQ also points to Wisconsin’s Fair Dealership Law. This guide does not resolve its applicability, exceptions, notice or cure requirements for a particular agreement. Preserve an independent contract review task even where the registration filing is straightforward.

sections.heading: The operating-law definition can lead to a different result
paragraphs: Chapter 135’s dealership/community-of-interest test is independent of the sales-registration process. The separate Fair Dealership Law guide tests in-state scope, exclusions, cause, notice/cure and marked-inventory issues. In particular, the nonpayment branch does not turn a 10-day cure notice into a universal day-11 termination right.

practicalOutput: A Wisconsin filing, disclosure and amendment calendar with no claim of merit approval.

title: Virginia: establish the exemption before relying on it
description: Virginia requires registration or an applicable exemption; some exemption routes require a filing before an offer or sale.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Exempt is a conclusion supported by facts
paragraphs: Virginia SCC states that franchises offered or sold in Virginia must be registered or exempt. Its overview says exemptions may depend on franchisor experience, financial condition or the characteristics of the offer or grant. It directs readers to 21 VAC 5-110-75 for conditions and filing requirements.

sections.heading: What an overseas management team should collect
paragraphs: Prepare the exact selling entity, relevant operating history, current financial statements, ownership chart, proposed buyer and transaction structure. Where a test concerns the franchisor, another group company’s trading history should not be substituted without establishing why the rule permits it.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a French service group
paragraphs: The parent has a long operating history but a newly incorporated subsidiary will grant U.S. rights. The expansion director records both entities separately. The exemption question stays unresolved until the responsible reviewer maps the selected route to the correct entity, evidence and pre-offer filing conditions.

sections.heading: A practical commitment gate
bullets: Record the precise exemption provision being assessed.
Identify each condition and which entity/person must meet it.
Assign missing evidence and any required filing before the covered event.
Retain the filing acknowledgement or the reason a self-executing route applies.
Separately review disclosure, advertising and ongoing relationship obligations; this overview does not resolve them.

sections.heading: Read the operative exemption rule
paragraphs: Current 21VAC5-110-75 sets different routes for unchanged uninterrupted renewal, additional existing-franchisee sales, seasoned franchisors, institutional buyers and substantial investment. The experienced parent is relevant only where the selected rule permits its facts and required guarantees. For routes 3–6, subdivision 7 still requires the disclosure document and all proposed agreements 14 calendar days before agreement or payment. A registration exemption is not a general disclosure waiver.

sections.heading: Make the Form H and renewal clocks specific
paragraphs: The seasoned and substantial-investment routes require the specified Form H package at least 10 business days before the covered offer/sale and have annual renewal rules; the institutional route calls for filing before each offer/sale. Material changes trigger exemption amendment. The specific annual routes say at least 10 business days before expiry, while paragraph 8(c)(1) says 10 days. Preserve both wordings and resolve the selected route before relying on the shorter reading. The regulation’s electronic-media wording does not establish the exclusive current filing channel.

sections.heading: Apply the July 2026 contract changes separately
paragraphs: The current Act and SCC’s April notice require a separate review of Virginia governing law and post-term retail-competition language, with the negotiated-sale exception. The separate Virginia contract guide covers the enacted scope and SCC amendment-before-sale instructions. Registration status and a group-history memorandum do not complete that task.

title: Rhode Island: registration and exemption notices have different anniversaries
description: Rhode Island’s active regulation measures registration from the initial effective date and exemption notices from receipt.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Two annual dates can differ
paragraphs: R.I. Gen. Laws 19-28.1-5 prohibits covered franchise offers or sales without registration or exemption. Active regulation 230-RICR-50-10-1.4 gives registration a 365-calendar-day period from its initial effective date. It gives an exemption a 365-day period from receipt of the notice. Filing, receipt and effectiveness are distinct dates.

sections.heading: Do not treat a fractional franchise as a label
paragraphs: The active regulation also sets out a fractional-franchise route with multiple conditions involving existing business experience, location, similarity, expected revenue share and control. It contains state-specific filing language. Those provisions need a coordinated review before relying on the route; a federal fractional exemption is not the answer to the state question.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a UK technical-service add-on
paragraphs: An established Rhode Island operator wants to add a branded service to its existing business. The brand records the operator’s existing business, experience, site, projected first-year mix and control facts. It leaves the exemption conditional until every relevant condition and required filing has been reviewed.

sections.heading: The company secretary’s calendar
bullets: Select registration or the exact exemption route.
Record application submission, actual receipt and effective date separately.
Identify which date controls the anniversary.
Preserve the reviewed rule version and exemption evidence.
Assign independent disclosure, advertising and operating-law review.

sections.heading: Define the relationship and the relevant connections
paragraphs: Section 19-28.1-3 uses a marketing-plan/brand/fee-in-excess-of-$500 test and a separate master-franchise alternative. Its wholesale exclusion refers to reasonable quantities of tangible goods. Section 4 separately tests offer/acceptance connections and an outside-state sale to a resident where the franchise will operate in Rhode Island. Outlet location alone does not exhaust the state screen.

sections.heading: Registration exemption and delivery exemption can differ
paragraphs: Section 8 requires a disclosure document reflecting all material changes and all proposed agreements at least 14 calendar days before execution or payment, subject to its listed exemption subsections. Active rule 1.5 separately describes a qualified fractional route exempting registration and delivery, with state-specific filing language. Identify the actual authority for both exemptions; one does not automatically establish the other.

sections.heading: Resolve the statutory default against the active rule
paragraphs: Section 9(d) gives a fiscal-year-based expiry default unless the director prescribes a different period by rule/order. Active rule 1.4 supplies the 365-day periods described above. The statute also calls for renewal filing 30 days before expiration. Section 11 separately requires prompt material-change amendments, so the next anniversary is not permission to wait after a material event.

practicalOutput: A Rhode Island filing log with the correct anniversary and conditional exemption analysis.
limitations: This guide reviews the stated franchise issue. Corporate tax, employment, operating permits and address-dependent requirements are separate research tasks.

title: South Dakota: notice filing does not mean no filing
description: South Dakota’s franchise notice law has pre-offer, completeness, annual renewal and continuing financial-reporting dimensions.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The statute calls it notice filing
paragraphs: SDCL 37-5B-4 prohibits a covered offer or sale unless properly notice filed or exempt. Section 37-5B-5 describes a complete filing with the FDD, application, consent to service and $250 initial fee. It generally becomes effective on receipt, subject to completeness and order/injunction provisions. Do not replace the actual receipt with an assumed mailing date.

sections.heading: Keep annual and financial events separate
paragraphs: The statute generally gives one year from receipt unless a different period is prescribed. It lists a $150 renewal fee and treats late filings as initial filings. It also requires notice within fifteen days after an auditor reaches the specified going-concern conclusion after effectiveness. The annual calendar will not catch every material financial event.

sections.heading: Advertising filing and truthful advertising are different
paragraphs: SDCL 37-5B-23 says advertisements need not be filed unless the director requests them. It also permits action against misleading advertising. “No routine advertising filing” should therefore be recorded narrowly; it does not support unsubstantiated revenue or profitability claims.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a German commercial-cleaning network
paragraphs: The CFO flags an auditor going-concern conclusion while the sales team is recruiting partners. The compliance owner records the conclusion date, the separate reporting task and any actual financial-assurance condition. The commercial team preserves advertising versions and substantiation rather than assuming a notice receipt approves the claims.

sections.heading: Commitment evidence
bullets: Complete filed package and actual receipt/effectiveness.
Exemption route and conditions if claimed.
Annual expiry and internal renewal date.
Auditor-event reporting owner.
Advertising evidence and any director request or order.

sections.heading: Add the delivery and receipt records
paragraphs: Sections 17–18 have an independent 14-calendar-day initial delivery rule and a seven-day unilateral material-agreement-change branch, subject to the actual exemptions. The prospect-initiated-negotiation language in 17(2) does not erase section 26(7)’s separate materially different signing-terms rule. Review both before setting the execution date. Section 18 distinguishes delivered/access instructions from first-class mailing, which must occur at least three days before the required delivery date. Section 11 requires a prospect-signed receipt before agreement/payment and seller retention for three years.

sections.heading: No ordinary update filing does not mean no update
paragraphs: Section 7 expressly says disclosure updating needs no division filing, while requiring a revised annual document within 120 days of fiscal close and reasonable-time quarterly material-change revisions. Prospects receive the most recent available quarterly revisions, and known financial-performance changes have a separate notice duty. Section 6 director-required amendments, annual notice renewal and the going-concern task remain independent.

practicalOutput: A South Dakota notice calendar and event-driven financial reporting task.
limitations: This guide reviews the stated franchise issue. Corporate tax, employment, operating permits and address-dependent requirements are separate research tasks.
No transaction-specific legal review has taken place. Record the offer locations, parties, model and planned dates before applying an exemption.

title: Connecticut: trace the registered mark through to the selling entity
description: The current trademark-exclusion claim asks who owns the mark and whether the seller can sublicense it; posting is not approval.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The current form asks a group-structure question
paragraphs: Form CT-BOIA-EX, effective September 30, 2025, describes a marketing-program exclusion claim involving a federally registered trademark or service mark. It asks whether the seller holds the mark, whether it has been assigned and whether the owner has licensed use and sublicensing to franchisees or purchasers. An overseas parent’s registration certificate alone may not show the selling subsidiary’s rights.

sections.heading: A filed claim is not validation
paragraphs: The form expressly says that the Department posts claims but cannot approve or validate them and that the seller bears the burden. The Department’s older guideline discusses certificates and supporting assignments/licences. Confirm the current filing route and requested evidence using the current form and agency directions; do not silently treat the older wording as the latest process.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a Malaysian parent and U.S. seller
paragraphs: The parent owns the brand, a Singapore group company has a regional licence and a new U.S. subsidiary will sell partner rights. The company secretary draws the chain of ownership, licensing territory and sublicense permission. Missing U.S. authority remains an unresolved document task; group ownership alone does not fill the gap.

sections.heading: Build a mark-rights packet
bullets: Federal registration identity, owner, relevant goods/services and status.
Exact entity proposing the Connecticut offer.
Signed assignment/licence chain and sublicense authority.
Reviewed exclusion grounds and any other definitional trigger.
Current filed claim, supporting evidence and responsible signatory.

sections.heading: Test the other definition limbs separately
paragraphs: The actual current official statutory mirror places the marketing-program trademark language in 36b-61(2)(D), consistent with the current form. Other limbs concern specified vending/display/amusement-device locations on third-party premises, product buyback, and stated income/refund guarantees. A mark-related marketing-program claim does not automatically answer a different limb. Section 65 places the exemption/exclusion/definition-exception burden on the claimant.

sections.heading: A covered non-exempt track has a different calendar
paragraphs: Under 36b-62, a covered non-exempt business opportunity is registered before offer/sale and becomes effective by commissioner order. Section 63 requires the actual disclosure at least ten business days before the earlier contract or money/thing-of-value event, with state cover/additional-content requirements even where a permitted federal-format document is used. Section 62(d) requires immediate material-change notice and appropriate disclosure amendment. Section 79 renews a registered opportunity within 120 days after fiscal close; those tasks do not automatically apply to a transaction properly outside that track.

sections.heading: A filing is not an advertising claim
paragraphs: Section 36b-67 separately requires documented data for income/earning-potential representations and disclosure of that data when the claims are made. It also addresses inconsistent advertising/oral claims and prohibits the specified references to compliance with the Act in advertising or other prospect contact. Preserve actual scripts, evidence and delivery dates; a registration or trademark claim does not validate the advertised returns. The selected definition and exact exemption scope still matter.

sections.heading: The relationship and premises law is independent
paragraphs: The separate Connecticut exit guide applies 42-133e through 42-133h’s own definition, cause/notice, lease-service and compensation rules. Those relationship provisions do not state the federal fee element, and a trademark exclusion filing does not decide their scope. The official base code and supplement index were read; later session laws and special sectors remain independent review tasks.

practicalOutput: A Connecticut mark-ownership and sublicense diagram with a documented claim review.
limitations: This page addresses its named decision, not a complete state legal survey. Unknown dimensions remain unresolved in the coverage register.
Model classification, state connections, sector-dealer laws, local requirements and the actual transaction need independent review. No sale, exemption, worker status or contract term is approved.

title: Florida: the annual franchise exemption filing still comes first
description: The agency removed registration-document requirements while retaining the annual franchise exemption notice.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Do not stop at the first agency sentence
paragraphs: FDACS says sellers of business franchises no longer file registration documents. Its next sentence says the Franchise Exemption filing remains. Current 2026 section 559.802 conditions the exemption on a qualifying federal-definition franchise, the notice stating substantial FTC compliance and payment of the set fee before the covered offer or sale.

sections.heading: Check both location and resident connections
paragraphs: The statute addresses a franchise to be located in Florida or a Florida resident. A prospect outside the proposed outlet state can therefore still be relevant. The notice is not replaced by forming a U.S. company, drafting an FDD or choosing a licence label.

sections.heading: Filing and renewal have their own dates
paragraphs: The statute gives the initial exemption one year from notice filing and allows annual renewal. It sets a fee ceiling of $100; that ceiling is not evidence of the current amount payable. The linked application packet required sign-in during this research, so the actual current filing fee and packet instructions remain a pre-filing confirmation task.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a German service brand
paragraphs: A Florida-resident partner proposes an operation elsewhere. The expansion manager records the resident and outlet facts separately, checks the applicable exemption and calendars the notice before a covered offer. The company secretary also records the anniversary, selling entity and FDD version.

sections.heading: Evidence to retain
bullets: Federal-definition/compliance analysis for the actual model.
Prospect residence and proposed outlet location.
Current agency form, actual fee and notice receipt.
One-year anniversary and renewal owner.
Independent advertising, sector and relationship-law questions.

sections.heading: A separate representation statute can still matter
paragraphs: Section 817.416 has an independent franchise/distributorship definition and intentional-misrepresentation rules for success prospects, known required investment and market capacity. The separate Florida representations guide tests the actual goods-supply/distribution facts and keeps the civil statutory showing separate from a prediction of recovery. A 559.802 annual exemption notice does not clear those claims.

practicalOutput: A Florida pre-offer notice and annual-renewal record.
limitations: This page addresses its named decision, not a complete state legal survey. Unknown dimensions remain unresolved in the coverage register.
